name: Hywel Dda
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.

text: Hywel Dda was a Welsh hero and king. He is also called Howel Dda, or Hywel the Good. He ruled the southwestern Welsh kingdom of Dyfed in the 10th century, from about 910 to 950 C.E. Hywel created an impressive body of law. It was codified in the late 12th century, or 13th by some sources, as Cyfraith Hywell, the Laws of Hywel. It was the first unified body of law in the land. Scholars often describe it as the Welsh parallel to the Irish Brehon laws. The Laws of Hywel Dda formed the basis of organized life in Wales for centuries. They set out the rights of the bards, the smiths, and the people. One law named poetry, clerkship, and smithcraft as the three arts a villein's son might not learn without his lord's consent. By binding the kingdom under one code, Hywel shaped the Welsh nation.

okr.objective: Document Hywel Dda, the Welsh king who created the first unified body of law.
